newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK STOCKS DIP ON HIGHER SHORT RATES, FX TURMOIL.
newsitem.headline: GREEK STOCKS DIP ON HIGHER SHORT RATES, FX TURMOIL.

text.p: Greek stocks weakened, falling victim to lingering doubts about higher short-term interbank rates linked to a softer drachma.
"Equities have been dealt a blow by soaring short-term rates which render them less attractive," said Evangelos Haratsis, managing director of Beta Securities.
He said there was uncertainty about the time required for the money and forex markets to cool down and in fact there was concern whether conditions would deteriorate.
"The market had risen on very light trade from retail investors in the past week and used the spike in interest rates as the excuse for profit-taking," said Haratsis.
Equities will look for a new equilibrium which will be closer to current price levels the sooner the turmoil is over with, he added.
The dollar was fixed at a record high against the drachma of 282.14 up from Wednesday's 281.5.
But the drachma gained ground against the ecu and was fixed at 309.85 from Wednesday's 309.92 with dealers saying that the central bank indicated it wanted ecu/drachma lower.
By fixing time (1330 local, 1030 GMT) the central bank had not moved in the forex market in support of the drachma, whereas in the previous day it had sold 660 million ecus and $60 million.
Depo rates continued to rise, with the one-month Athibor, Greece's reference rate, firming 40 basis points to 12.37 percent after Wednesday's 39 basis points rise.

"The market remains resilient in the face of sharp shifts in the external value of the drachma and interbank rates," Haratsis said. "It is certainly not overvalued and this will help equities recover from current fluctuations."
But he said neither Greece or other European countries had seen the last of currency and interest rate turmoil.

"This monetary crisis was the second for Greece during 1997 and many more took place around European Union countries," Haratsis said. "There is more to come as the time for Greece to join the ERM approaches."
The Athens general index settled 1.04 percent or 16.41 points lower than Wednesday's 1,572.87 close at 1,556.46 with all sector sub-indices save for insurance stocks registering losses.
Banks and industrials lost 1.27 and 0.75 percent respectively.
Turnover reached 14.1 billion drachmas on volume of 3.6 million shares, including active block trading in ErgoBank, with around 107,000 shares changing hands between 16,700 and 17,000 drachmas.
Decliners beat advancers 157 to 48 with 32 shares unchanged on 237 traded.
OTE telecom Global Depository Shares (GDS) were quoted on London's SEAQ International market at $10.6-$10.9. Two GDSs make up one share of OTE.
The Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 3,800 drachmas, capped at 5,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,112-1,142 drachmas.

The recently launched second Merrill Lynch call spread warrant on OTE with a strike price of 6,800 drachmas, capped at 10,000 drachmas, was quoted at 1,042-1,102 drachmas. The warrants expire December 16, 1998. Shares of the underlying stock shed 55 drachmas to 6,195.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $70.43-$73.18. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,314-3,532 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $11.58-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.
